faq.q: Can I download the spoken audio as an MP3 or WAV?
faq.a: No. This uses the browser's built-in Web Speech API, which provides no audio stream, so saving an MP3 or WAV is genuinely impossible here. The page is upfront about this and suggests recording the playback with the Screen Recorder tool if you need a file. What you can download is the text plus your voice settings as a .txt, or a ZIP of reading chunks.

faq.q: Why do the available voices differ between my devices?
faq.a: The voice list comes from your operating system and browser, not the tool, so Android, Windows, and iOS each offer a different set. You can search voices by name or language, and the dropdown groups them by language. Your chosen voice is remembered under tts_voice and reapplied, but if a saved voice isn't present on the current device it's skipped.

It reads each sentence aloud a set number of times (1 to 3, default 2) with a pause between them (1 to 15 seconds, default 4) so you can write along. It shows which sentence and repeat it's on, and prompts 'Write now...' during each pause. It's built for students practising dictation and works with the same voice, speed, pitch, and volume controls.

faq.q: How does it handle very long text and what are the presets?
faq.a: Long text is auto-split into chunks of up to about 200 characters on sentence and word boundaries, read in sequence with a progress bar and word highlighting. Five reading presets set speed and pitch: Natural (1.0x), Slow & clear (0.7x), Study pace (0.9x), Fast (1.5x), and Proofreading (0.8x, slightly higher pitch). Speed ranges 0.5x–2x. You can also upload a .txt/.md file up to 5MB.
